The test image shows corn kernels (seed part) with white cottony mycelium growing between them. The kernels are yellowish-orange/pinkish with no visible green or red mold. Candidates from the seed category: Aspergillus_Ear_Rot, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Gibberella_Disease, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot.

Now viewing one reference from each of 4 top candidates:

Analysis of the 4 reference images:

- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: Shows rotted cross-section with grayish-brown kernels, white mycelium at center — more compact/matted growth
- **Fusarium_Disease**: White fluffy mycelium growing between yellow-orange kernels — closely matches the test image (similar cottony white growth, similar kernel color/plumpness)
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Distinctly green/teal mold on kernels — does not match (test image has pure white mycelium)
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Pink/red mold at ear tip with husks adhering — does not match

The test image shows plump, yellowish-orange kernels with abundant white cottony mycelium between them, and a slight pinkish tinge to the kernels. This matches Fusarium_Disease best: whitish to pink fungal growth, fluffy white mycelium on and between kernels. Trichoderma and Gibberella are ruled out by color. Diplodia typically starts at the base and produces more matted, grayish mycelium.
